message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and placed one buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 (~$9,801 total, within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no money left the account). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS — figures I confirmed both in Apple's own newsroom release and in the trusted SEC 10-K lookup (filed 2024-11-01). I deliberately discarded a blog post (fin-data-live.net) claiming "corrected" FY24 revenue of $352.9B, since it contradicts both Apple's press release and its 10-K and offered no verifiable sourcing. News flow around the print was neutral-to-constructive — shares were steady as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout — so with the stock at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and roughly 36.6x trailing EPS, I sized a modest starter position rather than a full allocation, keeping the limit price essentially at market as the mandate requires.
